prompt.context: Over the past five years, the government of Saudi Arabia has been focused on reducing economic dependence on oil by diversifying the domestic economy. As part of this effort, the government has evidenced a willingness to relax certain social norms. As part of the diversification initiative, the government hired us to forecast the potential revenue impact of taxing shisha consumption.
prompt.question: What is the estimated revenue impact of legalizing and taxing public shisha consumption for the Saudi government over a three-year period?

clarifying_info.a: Shisha is an instrument for vaporizing and smoking flavored tobacco. In the Arab world and Middle East, people smoke waterpipes as part of the cultural traditions.

clarifying_info.q: How will the Saudi government make money off of shisha?
clarifying_info.a: Institutions must apply and pay for an annual license to sell shisha. Additionally, sales tax and import tariffs are levied by the government as appropriate.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a specific revenue target in mind?
clarifying_info.a: No, the Saudi government only wishes to maximize revenue over a 3-year period.

clarifying_info.q: How much revenue does the Saudi government currently earn?
clarifying_info.a: 2.5 trillion Saudi riyal annually. Tobacco and other related products currently generate 500 million SAR in revenue.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any social norms we should be aware of?
clarifying_info.a: Islam is widely practiced by Saudi citizens and governs their personal, political, economic and legal lives. Additionally, public consumption of shisha is currently banned but is widely consumed at home.

exhibits.title: Riyadh restaurant market segmentation
exhibits.shows: A table breaking down Riyadh's restaurant market by type, with number of businesses and U.S. market equivalents. Footnotes state Riyadh represents ~20% of the domestic restaurant market and the average restaurant lifespan is three years.

framework: Revenue Sources: Licenses (type/quantity of businesses, one-time vs. annual fees, adoption rate over 3 years, restaurant lifespan), Sales Tax (consumer segments, spending habits, adoption rate, tax rate), Import Tariffs (domestic vs. foreign sourced shisha, tariff percentage)
Cost Considerations: Regulatory body setup, auditing and quality control, implementation vs. ongoing costs
Social Issues: Public opinion on legalizing public consumption, health and well-being of citizens, job creation

questions.prompt: Which licensing structure should Saudi Arabia adopt, and what is the estimated three-year revenue impact from licenses?
questions.guidance: Candidates should first compare the three-year cumulative value of each license structure per restaurant: Qatar one-time 10k = 10k total; Jordan 3k one-time + 500/month x 12 x 3 = 3k + 18k = 21k total; UAE 6k one-time + 3k/year x 3 = 6k + 9k = 15k total. Jordan maximizes revenue at 21k per restaurant over 3 years. Then apply Jordan's structure to Riyadh's restaurant base with the given adoption rates and new restaurant additions to get total Riyadh revenue, then scale to domestic (x5). Great candidates will also contextualize: the initiative adds ~17.1% to the existing 500M SAR tobacco revenue.

math.setup: Jordan license: 3,000 SAR one-time fee + 500 SAR/month (= 6,000 SAR/year). Total Riyadh restaurants: Year 1 = 14,000 (baseline), Year 2 = 15,000 (+1,000 new), Year 3 = 16,000 (+1,000 new). Adoption rates: Year 1 = 5%, Year 2 = 10%, Year 3 = 15%. Newly participating each year = incremental participating restaurants. One-time fee charged only to newly participating restaurants each year. Annual fee charged to all participating restaurants.
steps: One-time fee revenue (millions SAR): Y1 = 700 x 3,000 = 2.10M; Y2 = 800 x 3,000 = 2.40M; Y3 = 900 x 3,000 = 2.70M
Total Riyadh license revenue: Y1 = 6.30M; Y2 = 11.40M; Y3 = 17.10M; 3-year total = 34.80M SAR
Scale to domestic (Riyadh = 20%, so x5): 34.80M x 5 = 174M SAR over 3 years; Year 3 annualized domestic = 17.10M x 5 = 85.5M SAR
Context: 85.5M SAR represents a 17.1% increase over the existing 500M SAR tobacco revenue baseline
math.answer: Jordan's structure maximizes revenue. Estimated domestic license revenue over 3 years is ~174M SAR, with Year 3 run-rate reaching ~85.5M SAR annually — a ~17.1% uplift to existing tobacco-related revenue.

brainstorming.prompt: Are there any other considerations the Saudi government should keep in mind before legalizing the public consumption of shisha?

categories.name: Health & Social
ideas: Health and well-being of citizens given increased consumption of tobacco products
Public opinion — restaurants may not want to sell shisha and patrons may not want to smoke in public
Reputation on the global stage, as many countries are restricting use of tobacco products

categories.name: Revenue Upside
ideas: Revenues related to sales tax on shisha product purchases
Import tariff revenue on foreign-sourced shisha products
Three-year economic forecast to stress-test adoption rate assumptions

categories.name: Distribution & Operations
ideas: Other distribution channels to sell shisha beyond restaurants (e.g., dedicated lounges, hotels, retail)
Associated costs with launching and governing the licensing program

categories.name: Economic Opportunity
ideas: Job creation related to the budding shisha industry
Potential for domestic shisha manufacturing to reduce import reliance

recommendation: Adopt Jordan's licensing structure (3,000 SAR one-time fee + 500 SAR/month) as it maximizes three-year per-restaurant revenue at 21,000 SAR vs. Qatar at 10,000 SAR and UAE at 15,000 SAR
Estimated domestic license revenue over the three-year period is approximately 174M SAR, with Year 3 generating ~85.5M SAR — a 17.1% increase over current tobacco-related revenues of 500M SAR
Note that these figures are conservative as they exclude sales tax and import tariff revenue streams
risks: License revenue depends heavily on the assumed adoption rate (5%/10%/15%); lower adoption significantly reduces revenue
Healthcare costs related to increased tobacco consumption could offset fiscal gains
Restaurants and patrons may resist public shisha consumption due to cultural or religious sensitivities
next_steps: Conduct market analysis of restaurants' willingness to sell shisha to validate adoption rate assumptions
Explore and quantify financial and social costs related to the regulatory program
Model additional revenue streams from sales tax and import tariffs to complete the full revenue picture
